main_text.l: tam palam est, vt huius rei causa nullius Philosophi schola intranda sit, haec Seneca 4.Naturalium 7.in f.
11. De lege Iulia repetundarum, & corrupto iudice.
De Iudice qui ob rem dicendam pecuniam accepserit, dixi s.ad Titul.dei udiciis.
Dixi s.ad Titulum de Possessionibus & interdictis.

Sanates dicti sunt, qui supra infraque Romam habitauerunt, quia cum defecissent a Romanis, breui post redierunt in amicitiam, quasi sanata mente. Itaque in xii. cautum est, Vt{*} idem{b} iuris esset sanatibus, quod fortibus [quidam legunt fortibus] id est bonis, & qui nunquam defecerunt a populo Romano, Festus in sanates.

marginalia.note: * Iosephus apud Festum in Sanates ita restituit, Nexosoluto que, forcti sanatique idem ius esto. i, bono Romano idè & peregrino qui inferiore loco est, hæc ille. Alias de sanatibus populis opiniones, videapud eundé d.loco.
haec particula mouit me, vti hocce put referrem ad Titulû de captiuis. quod vix improbabunt, qui huic loco contulerint legem 7. ff.de captiuis.

page.notes: Marginal marks are uncertain: the mark after "Vt" is read as an asterisk, and the "*" and "b" notes are read from the printed marks. The note beside the first lines ("quaterentur ...") and the "d.loco" reference are set in very small type and may be misread. "forcti" is doubtful, and the printed reading of "Ne-xosoluto" across the line break is uncertain. The gathering signature "H 2" is faint. Long s is normalised to s; "eft" is transcribed as est. Printing errors such as "Vt" for "Ut" are left as printed. The "11." and "12." lines are treated as titles of level 3; the division "De captiuis." is level 2.
